title: prefetch-wave-gate-reservoir-and-decode-resequencer
author: Samira Khan
description: Motivation: reduce decode-stage jitter and KV cache thrashing caused by bursty arrival patterns while preserving throughput. This PR implements a lightweight buffered wave-gating layer (wave-gate) between the prefetch/prefill stage and decode kernels, a small reservoir that smooths microburst handoffs, and a resequencer that reorders micro-slices for better KV cache locality. The goal is to improve tail latency (P95/P99) under mixed workloads and busy multi-tenant GPUs without changing kernel semantics.

release_notes: Introduces 'wave-gate' buffering to smooth prefetch-to-decode handoffs, an adaptive reservoir for burst smoothing, and a decode resequencer that improves KV cache locality. Expected P95 latency reductions in mixed workloads and improved cost efficiency for high-concurrency tenants.
perf_benchmarks: KV cache hit-rate: +6.2% on representative e2e traces
Cost estimate: token-cost-per-req reduced ~5.9% due to fewer wasted KV fetches
testing_summary: Unit tests cover WaveGate admission and backpressure, resequencer correctness under out-of-order microchunks, and policy adaptor permutations. Integration tests validate end-to-end prefill->wave-gate->decode path and ensure no deadlocks under saturation. CI runs included perf workflow with 3 representative workloads.
notes_for_reviewers: Key areas to scrutinize: admission watermark tuning (defaults chosen conservatively), race conditions in resequencer ordering, and interactions with existing KV soft-evict heuristics. I added feature flags to gate the resequencer and reservoir separately for staged rollout.
review_conversation: Luis Ortega: Nice design sketch. Can we avoid copying payloads when moving slices into the WaveGate? Consider zero-copy handoff.
Samira Khan: Addressed in a1f3b9d — added reference-counted slice wrapper to enable zero-copy in common paths; fallbacks remain for edge cases.
Mina Patel: The reservoir watermark defaults seem low for large-token flows; do we have safe guards to avoid head-of-line blocking?
Samira Khan: Added adaptive watermarks with a max-latency guard and added a per-request bypass path for latency-critical SLA-tagged requests. See reservoir.rs lines ~120-180.
Ethan Zhao: Could resequencing violate model ordering expectations for chat sessions? Need explicit session affinity check.

Samira Khan: Resequencer checks request session ids and will preserve strict order for session-affine streams; resequencing only applies to independent micro-slices across different sessions or non-affine continuations.
Mina Patel: CI perf run looks promising. Please add a short note to ops runbook about toggling the feature flags if we see regressions in damage-control windows.
Samira Khan: Added ops note and a debug endpoint that exports WaveGate internals for live troubleshooting.
merge_details: Merged by Mina Patel via squash-merge. Commit message summarizes wave-gate + reservoir + resequencer and points to ENG-4412.
deployment_notes: Feature gated: wave_gate_enabled (default on for canary nodes), resequencer_enabled (default off). Gradual rollout recommended: enable wave_gate first on canary pool, monitor P95/P99 and KV hit-rate, then enable resequencer for non-sessioned workloads.
